chapter: The 1949 band, breakup and later years
title: The 1949 band's trumpet section
summary: The 1949 section of Johnny Howell, Ray Wetzel, Maynard Ferguson, Doc Severinsen and Ralph Ericson impressed Harry James at Bop City.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: You were telling me, I think it was at dinner -- I don't think we have this on the tape -- about that out of sight trumpet section. We didn't get that on the tape, did we?
Tell me about that trumpet section.
Oh, that's right, we were talking about John Howell, and that's how it came up.

Yeah. The '49 band, the trumpet section was Johnny Howell, Ray Wetzel, Maynard Ferguson, Doc Severinsen and Ralph Ericson. And it was something to hear, that trumpet section. They all made a contribution. Like Ray Wetzel was the disciplinarian of the group. I mean he'd say do it like this. And they respected Ray, believe me. This included Maynard and they respected his generalship. Of course Maynard had his thing and Doc had his thing and Ralph had his thing,
and then Johnny had his thing, but they respected Ray, and Ray ran -- actually was the general. And they did some remarkable things. I know Harry James came into Bop City and heard them and --
That's right, that band played Bop City in June, 1949.
I don't know, it was somewhere in there.

And Harry told me, he said, 'I never heard a trumpet section like this in my life. It's unbelievable.' Of course you're crazy, really, in a way, to get a trumpet section like that, because you know you're not going to keep these guys. They're going to peel off into their own thing and you're going to be left with a bunch or arrangements that nobody can play.
But what an experience while it's happening.
Oh, it's just wonderful to have had them.
